rows.obligation: TASA s 30-10 Code item 6; TPB(GS) 55/2026 ¶¶23–25: client permission before AI use
rows.meaning: Entering client information into an AI tool can be a disclosure to a third party, depending on how the tool is configured and used, so client permission may be needed first.
rows.design: A data note says which providers see client data and where it's processed.
rows.evidence: A one-page data note naming each processor, its region and its retention setting

rows.obligation: APESB Technical Alert (31 Oct 2025): APES 110 applies to AI use
rows.meaning: Members using AI must keep meeting APES 110 and critically assess and verify AI-generated information, and the APESB says they should disclose and supervise AI use.
rows.design: Every register field links to its page, so a reviewer can check it.
rows.evidence: A register with a source-page link per field, and a test report listing every miss

rows.obligation: Privacy (Tax File Number) Rule 2015 ss 10, 11: use limits and safeguards for TFNs
rows.meaning: Every holder of TFN information, whatever its size, may use or disclose it only for tax, superannuation or personal-assistance law purposes (or to give individuals their own TFN information), and must take reasonable steps to protect it.
rows.design: TFNs are masked before any model call unless the job needs the field.
rows.evidence: A masking test result that lists any TFN left unmasked

rows.obligation: Privacy Act APPs 6 and 11: personal information entered into AI products
rows.meaning: For practices the APPs cover (generally turnover over $3m; smaller ones only in listed cases), putting personal information into an AI product is a use or disclosure under APP 6, and APP 11 requires reasonable security steps.
rows.design: Where the provider offers the setting, tools are set so it doesn't train on what you enter.
rows.evidence: An onshore note stating where inference runs and what the provider retains

rows.obligation: AML/CTF Act s 28 (from 1 Jul 2026 for table 6 services): initial CDD for a trust customer
rows.meaning: A practice providing AUSTRAC-regulated services, such as setting up or restructuring a trust, must establish a trust customer's trustees, beneficiaries or their classes, and beneficial owners, among other matters. AUSTRAC names the deed and deeds of variation for verifying the trust's details, not individuals' identities.
rows.design: Each role links to its deed page; your AML/CTF compliance officer signs off.
rows.evidence: A trust register with a page link per field, and an exception list
